title: LightmapGI bakes lights under SubViewport with 'own_world_3d' on
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in [4.6.2.stable] and [4.7.beta3]

### System information

Godot v4.7.beta3 - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sun, 17 May 2026 17:23:07 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT (RADV NAVI22) - AMD Ryzen 7 5800X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.22 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Surround 3.1)

### Issue description

This is technically less of a bug and more of a question regarding intended scope.

When baking lightmaps with LightmapGI it also bakes the 3D lights that are children of a SubViewport with 'own_world_3d' enabled. I would expect it to not bake those lights as it is its own 3D world.

Technically it makes sense that LightmapGI chooses to include those lights in the bake if the SubViewport node is a sibling or a child of LightmapGI. The question is more of whether the scope of the bake should extend into the 'own_world_3d'. I would expect it not to because the inherent reason to enable it in the first place is to have a separate 3D world in the same scene. Hence I wouldn't want the lights from the separate 3D world bleeding into the main one.

### Steps to reproduce

In the MRP you can see that LightmapGI bakes the OmniLight that is the child of the SubViewport. That light's bake mode is set to static. If it is set to disabled it does not bake.
